newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Kian Ann taps Asia infrastructure growth.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Kian Ann taps Asia infrastructure growth.

text.p: Heavy equipment, machinery and diesel engine parts distributor Kian Ann Engineering Ltd is relying on Southeast Asia's infrastructure spending to fuel its growth in the next few years, company officials said on Monday.

Kian Ann, which announced earlier on Monday it was offering 30 million shares at Singapore S$0.60 each in its Singapore initial public offering (IPO), said its business was closely linked to infrastructure development in Asia.
The company distributes parts of heavy machinery like bulldozers, excavators, trucks, power generation sets and marine engines. It hopes its IPO will raise net proceeds of about S$16.5 million.

"The ASEAN economy, which is our main market, is expected to grow 7.7 percent per annum for the next five years. The infrastructure expenditure for the next 10 years will go to almost US$500 billion," Chew Thiam Keng, general manager and executive director of Kian Ann told reporters at the IPO launch. This spending will translate into strong demand for excavators, bulldozers and other equipment used in building infrastructure
and in turn demand for Kian Ann's products, Chew said.

He said the company was looking to setting up offices and warehouses in the countries where it sells its products, in particular Malaysia and Indonesia. Presently, its warehousing facilities are located in Singapore.
Kian Ann distributes 500,000 products covering 150 brands and intends to increase its product range with its IPO proceeds.

For the financial year ended June 30, 1996, 63 percent of Kian Ann's turnover of S$63.14 million was generated outside Singapore. Overseas markets contributed 47 percent of its pre-tax profit of S$7.14 million during that period.

Most of Kian Ann's earnings come from sale of parts to the industrial sector where pre-tax profit margins are about 11.6 percent, compared to gross margins of 4.7 percent for the sale of parts to the marine sector, the company's prospectus said.
Officials said the company's main competitor was Malaysian-listed Triumphal Associates Berhad.
They said there were tough barriers to entry into the heavy equipment parts business as it required extensive product knowledge and a high capital investment.
